title: Joshua 21:1–8
context: After the tribal allotments and the cities of refuge (Joshua 13–20), the Levites ask for the towns Moses had commanded for them (Numbers 35). The cities are assigned by lot to the Kohathite, Gershonite, and Merarite families.

verses.text: Then the heads of fathers’ houses of the Levites came near to Eleazar the priest, and to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the heads of fathers’ houses of the tribes of the children of Israel.
verses.arminianNotes: The Levite family heads approach Eleazar, Joshua, and the tribal leaders. Arminian readers see the Levites taking responsible initiative to claim what God had already promised them through Moses.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s earlier word governing the request. The scene shows priestly and civil leaders working together to carry out what the LORD had commanded for the tribe set apart for his service.

verses.text: They spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, “The LORD commanded through Moses to give us cities to dwell in, with their pasture lands for our livestock.”
verses.arminianNotes: At Shiloh the Levites say, “The LORD commanded through Moses to give us cities to dwell in.” Arminian readers see God’s people appealing to his promise as the ground of their request.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the request resting entirely on God’s prior command, recorded in Numbers 35. The Levites do not ask for favors but for the fulfillment of what God himself had appointed for them.

verses.text: The children of Israel gave to the Levites out of their inheritance, according to the commandment of the LORD, these cities with their pasture lands.
verses.arminianNotes: Israel gives the Levites cities from its own inheritance, as the LORD commanded. Arminian readers see willing obedience by the tribes, who share what they received so that God’s servants can live among them.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the tribes honoring God’s command by giving from their portion. The land remains God’s gift, and the tribes act as stewards when they set aside cities for the Levites.

verses.text: The lot came out for the families of the Kohathites. The children of Aaron the priest, who were of the Levites, had thirteen cities by lot out of the tribe of Judah, out of the tribe of the Simeonites, and out of the tribe of Benjamin.
verses.arminianNotes: The first lot falls to the Kohathites, and Aaron’s descendants receive thirteen cities from Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin. Arminian readers see orderly provision that places the priests near the heartland of the tribes.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the lot as a means by which God directs the allotment. Proverbs 16:33 expresses the conviction that the decision of the lot comes from the LORD, which fits the way this chapter proceeds.

verses.text: The rest of the children of Kohath had ten cities by lot out of the families of the tribe of Ephraim, out of the tribe of Dan, and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh.
verses.arminianNotes: The remaining Kohathites receive ten cities from Ephraim, Dan, and half of Manasseh. Arminian readers see each Levitical family provided for, so that no part of the tribe is left without a home.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s care extending to every clan of Levi. The careful numbering shows that the distribution is complete and fair, matching the instructions Moses had given.

verses.text: The children of Gershon had thirteen cities by lot out of the families of the tribe of Issachar, out of the tribe of Asher, out of the tribe of Naphtali, and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
verses.arminianNotes: The Gershonites receive thirteen cities from Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and half of Manasseh in Bashan. Arminian readers see Levites spread through the northern tribes, where they could teach and serve God’s people.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the dispersion of Levi throughout Israel. Genesis 49:7 had spoken of Levi being scattered in Israel, and here that scattering takes the form of service among all the tribes.

verses.text: The children of Merari according to their families had twelve cities out of the tribe of Reuben, out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun.
verses.arminianNotes: The Merarites receive twelve cities from Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun. Arminian readers see even the tribes east of the Jordan sharing their land with the Levites, binding the nation together in worship.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see provision reaching across the Jordan. The inclusion of Reuben and Gad anticipates chapter 22, where the unity of the tribes on both sides of the river is tested.

verses.text: The children of Israel gave these cities with their pasture lands by lot to the Levites, as the LORD commanded by Moses.
verses.arminianNotes: Israel gives these cities by lot, “as the LORD commanded by Moses.” Arminian readers see the community completing its obligation faithfully and carrying out God’s word in concrete detail.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the refrain stressing obedience to God’s command through Moses. The summary closes the overview before the detailed list, confirming that the process followed God’s instructions.
